payload.label: L5-F1
payload.text: Headline states 'Claude Code records acts exhaustively and reasoning almost not at all' as universal fact, but rests on single-machine, single-user measurement (5,754 blocks from one install on 2026-07-18). Binary findings are reproducible; empirical findings are not. Scope should be hedged inline.

payload.label: L5-F2
payload.text: Case against acknowledges: "If reasoning traces are unreliable, that is an argument against the whole enterprise including the artifact-based substitute we recommend" (line 80-84). Recommendation then claims artifacts are better but admits they are "still self-report, so it buys durability and non-circularity, not sincerity" (line 410). Logical gap: if both thinking-blocks and artifact-records are self-report subject to post-hoc rationalization, the recommendation does not solve the faithfulness problem—it relocates it. Report does not explain why durability matters if content is rationalized, or defend the move beyond "we control the format." Missing argument for the superiority of the proposed solution.

payload.label: L5-F3
payload.text: Report claims artifact-based recording is "checkable by an adversary against the artifact it cites" (line 407). But auditor who reads agent's record "I declined avenue X because [reason]" faces the same verification burden as reading a thinking-block summary: is the stated reason honest? Report does not explore how artifacts are verified for accuracy. If verification is "by adversary review," verification cost is not cheaper than reading thinking blocks—it is instead higher (more prose to read) plus the burden that the agent was expected to write it down honestly. Recommendation treats artifact-writing as a substitute for telemetry but does not address whether adjudication harnesses have fewer verification tasks or merely different ones.

payload.label: L5-F4
payload.location: Lines of inquiry, line 31-33 vs Open Questions, line 481
payload.text: Report identifies showThinkingSummaries experiment as 'the single experiment that could overturn the headline' but declines to run it citing state-modification outside seat consent. Decline is framed as governance issue but lacks rigorous risk/benefit tradeoff. If experiment is the only thing that moves the needle and cost is one settings mutation plus rerun, decline deserves stronger justification or escalation. Report carries it as open question but frames decline as consent issue rather than risk/benefit issue.

payload.label: L5-F5
payload.text: Report treats 'omitted' display mode as limitation or design choice that is unfortunate for adjudication. Does not explore whether 'omitted' is intentional privacy-by-design, or whether enabling thinking summaries might leak sensitive reasoning to API summary models. Report assumes reader wants thinking capture; does not consider that 'omitted' might be correct default from user-privacy perspective. Frames analysis one-sidedly without exploring whether 'reasoning not captured' is a problem or a feature.

payload.label: L5-F6
payload.text: Soundness tier system is clear for individual observations but does not address composite claims spanning multiple tiers. Example: 'agent chose tool X correctly' mixes Tier 1 (choice is observable) with Tier 4 (correctness requires external oracle). Report provides no rule for composing tiers or warning about cross-tier claims. Affects how findings should be graded; not a defect in report's own use but a gap in framework for consumers.

payload.label: L5-F7
payload.text: Risk matrix enumerates failure modes of telemetry capture, transcripts, and tool truncation but omits a failure mode of the recommended artifact-based solution: agents write what they believe auditors want to see, verification cost equals or exceeds thinking-block verification cost. Given that entire recommendation rests on artifact-based recording, risk matrix should include failure mode of that mechanism. Report acknowledges artifacts are self-report (line 410) but does not risk-grade strategic dishonesty in self-report.

payload.label: L5-F8
payload.text: Phrase 'no configuration of the OpenTelemetry surface will ever yield reasoning' uses absolute language, but report elsewhere emphasizes all findings are version-bound to Claude Code v2.1.215 and that redaction is 'unconditional map' that could be changed in future release. Section 9 lists 'Vendor changes default again' as medium-likelihood risk. Claim should be hedged to 'no configuration in v2.1.215 will yield reasoning.' Absolute language creates false permanence in transient system.

payload.label: L5-F9
payload.text: Report lists as stopping point 'if working showThinkingSummaries capture is demonstrated on non-interactive session, reorient.' Complementary counterfactual not explored: if future version flips default from 'omitted' to 'summarized' without requiring code change (per #32810 history, server-side flips happen). Would require entire headline and recommendation to be redone. Listed as risk in matrix but not carried as proactive stopping point or monitoring practice.
